main_text.l: eum est in encomio Helenæ, & Pana-thenaicâ, à Theseo popularem statum esse introductum, & ad ejus formam à posteris eundem restitutum? quomodò à Plutarcho hoc ipso loco, noluisse eum democratiam suam confusam esse?quo-modò à Pausaniâ in Atticis, Thesea popularis status fuisse autorem?Quæ enim populi partes in civitate, si jure suffragii in creandis magistratibus & negociis similibus destituatur? Sed hoc in medio relinquo. Ad cætera me confero, quæ ex Plutarcho clarent. Theseus his in populum collatis se penè regio jure exuit, nomen modò regis, & custodiam legum institutorumque,ac imperium mi-litare[?] cum dignitate, sicuti promiserat, sibi reservavit: abolitis prytaneis, & curiis & magistratibus oppidorum aliorum, unum prytaneum commune, curiam unam, (βουλευτήριον[?] vocat Plu-tarchus[?]) constituit Athenis eo loco, ubi tempore Plutarchi adhuc erat. In ha-c[?] in rerum memoriam ab ipso solenne festum institutum esse, diversi autores prodidêre, quod [illegible, ~7 letters] à navigatio-nis[?], συνοίκια à cohabitatione, [illegible, ~6 letters] à celebritate cunctis Athenien-sibus communi dixêre, quotannis die xvi mensis Hecatombæonis instauran-dum.

page.notes: Left margin: several short marginal fragments (for example "avit:", "Ialt:", "ivit") are partly hidden by a red stain and are only partly legible; the one transcribed as a note is the most certain. "mi-litare" is a line-end word hidden by the stain; the completion "litare" is a guess. The Greek in the brackets ("βουλευτήριον", "Plutarchus") is partly obscured, and the second Greek word in the line "ἀπὸ ... navigatio-" and the third Greek word are illegible. The word "ac[?]" at the start of the line after "navigatio-" is uncertain. "xvi" is printed in small capitals. "Thesea" in the printed text has a stray Cyrillic-like letter risk; read as "Theseo" in the line "Theseo popularem". The spacing "cunctis Athenien-" is printed with a gap.
